This update records the executed fact, asserts the scoped runtime consumption defect it exposes, and requests a successor execution whose comparison admission carries a common identity field so the controller can evaluate the predicate directly (the first run's comparisons were unknown only because the admission alias lacked ready.from/ready.start_from).

knowledge.statement: With decided=6 and compacted=4 on the executed two-node log, read_decided_suffix(1) returned exactly [Trimmed(4), Decided(5), Decided(6)] (len 3) although decided-from is 5, while read_decided_suffix(4) returned [Decided(5), Decided(6)] (len 2). The trimmed prefix is represented by a single Trimmed element, so the returned vector length is not the number of requested log indices when the start is below the compacted index.
knowledge.conditions: Two OmniPaxos instances (pids 1,2) built from ClusterConfig {configuration_id:1, nodes:[1,2]}, MemoryStorage, batch_size 1, no snapshots; node 1 becomes leader via try_become_leader, appends Value(1..=6) with full message delivery after each append, then trims to 4 and the trim is forwarded to node 2; both nodes report decided 6.

knowledge.statement: Applied to those real read_decided_suffix outputs, one cursor step per returned element (the actor's push_to_sub rule) leaves next_idx at 4 after the catch-up from 1, and the next push_to_all_subs read from 4 yields entries 5 and 6 again, so the delivered value sequence is 5,6,5,6 with duplicates of 5 and 6 while decided remains 6 and no new entry was decided.

The replay is a reconstruction of the runtime source logic over executed core outputs, not an execution of the runtime crate.

interpretations.rationale: The executed run establishes the decisive operands (receipt 8572576b3ff04353ac08bce770a5ad51, parsed events 0-3, test decided_suffix_collapses_trimmed_prefix passed, exit 0). Event 0 shows the setup was real: node 1 is leader in Accept, both nodes decided 6, compacted 4. Event 1 shows read_decided_suffix(1) returned kinds trimmed,decided,decided with tokens T4,5,6 and len 3 while decided_minus_from is 5, so a trimmed prefix of four indices is collapsed into one element. Event 2 shows the aligned case at from=4 (len 2). Event 3 applies the runtime's own cursor rule from source, one increment per returned element, to those real reads: cursor_after_catchup is 4, the next push reads from 4 and returns tokens 5,6, and delivered_values is 5,6,5,6 with duplicate_values 5,6 while decided stays 6. Nothing new was decided between the two reads, so the re-delivery is caused by the cursor arithmetic alone. The runtime therefore violates its documented single in-order decided stream for a subscriber whose next_idx is below the compacted index: subscribe_decided accepts any from and neither rejects a compacted start nor advances the cursor to decided after a collapsed catch-up, and a lagging subscriber crosses the same boundary. An application applying Decided entries to its state machine would apply entries 5 and 6 twice. The three declared EventComparisons reported unknown solely because my admission alias ready lacked the identity fields from/start_from the comparisons key on; the measured fields were fully observed, and a successor execution with a shared run identity is requested to make the predicate evaluation explicit.
counterevidence: A subscriber that only starts at or after the compacted index is aligned: event 2 shows from=4 yields exactly two elements for two indices, so the defect is limited to a cursor below the compacted index.

The Trimmed element is a documented LogEntry variant carrying the compacted index, so delivering it is correct; the defect is only the one-step-per-element increment that treats it as a single log index.
limitations: omnipaxos_runtime is not a dev-dependency of the omnipaxos test target, so the actor cannot be compiled or run here; events 1-2 measure the core read shape and event 3 is a faithful replay of the actor's source arithmetic over that output, not an actor execution.
Only one compaction point, no snapshots, no batching and a single subscriber are exercised; snapshot-based compaction yields a Snapshotted element under the same collapse but was not executed.
